title: Methods & Results: build, review and export a draft
description: Open the nested reporting tool, build a digest from the real completed Regression example, identify three concrete review problems and preserve an explicitly unreviewed Markdown export.
objectives: Find Methods & Results inside Regression and supply the correct completed-run sources.
Distinguish recorded analysis facts from inferred defaults, exporter metadata and candidate wording.
Copy the displayed sections and export an unchanged draft with its structured digest.
Understand why successful export and AI number checks are not scientific approval.
prerequisite: Complete the downloaded-data Regression example first; keep its original project, run journal and guide_permutation results. This is a review-and-export lesson, NOT a scientifically approved manuscript or an application fix. The recorded run journal declares guide_permutation_seed=0 but no global random_seed; the draft separately resolves seed=42. These are not interchangeable generator identities, and the recording does not establish which global seed was applied. The original analysis environment records spaCR 1.5.0.4, while the new draft names exporter version 1.5.0.5; do not relabel the historic run. All 325 saved gene-family BH values were independently checked: no q<0.05 and minimum q=0.2708333333333333. Ten displayed candidates have matching effects/p/q, but the 'strongest hits' heading does not make them significant; not every guide count or scientific assumption is certified. The genuine Copy sections and Export Markdown actions preserve the original prose and exact digest; the new file is named UNREVIEWED_methods_results.md. All original and private input hashes remain unchanged. No provider is contacted, no regression is rerun, no manuscript is approved and nothing is published. API: spacr.methods_export.build_digest, render_methods and render_results. The earlier strict scientific-accuracy hold is preserved separately.

scenes.narration: Open Regression from Home, then its nested Methods and Results tool. This tutorial belongs under Regression in the submodule section. It uses the real completed example from the Regression lesson, not invented results. The goal here is to build, inspect and preserve a draft, not to approve a manuscript automatically.

Choose the project folder, the particular run journal, and that run's regression-results folder. Leave Classifier empty because this example is reporting a regression run, not a classifier checkpoint. Keep the original files unchanged. Matching names are not enough: confirm that the journal and results describe the same completed run.

Click Build digest. Methods, Results, Caveats and Run digest are generated without contacting an AI provider. These sections are a starting point for review. In this recording the prose names the exporter's version, while the original run records a different analysis version. Report the version that actually produced the analysis.

Read the caveats rather than treating a successful build as validation. Here the generic seed sentence says forty-two. The original journal explicitly declares the permutation seed as zero, but does not declare a global run seed. Do not replace every forty-two with zero: first distinguish the generators and their recorded provenance.

The Run digest tab lets you inspect those structured records. Compare declared settings and the saved environment against the prose. A default inferred during export is not proof of historical execution. Preserve warnings and unresolved questions, including missing quality-control information; an absent report is not evidence that quality control passed.

The saved gene table contains three hundred twenty-five tests and none is significant at a q-value threshold of zero point zero five. Its smallest q-value is about zero point two seven. The heading strongest hits is therefore misleading here: these are ranked candidates, not discoveries. Check the complete corrected family, not only attractive top rows.

Copy sections copies the displayed Methods and Results together. It does not correct their wording, certify their numbers or include the structured appendix. Preserve an unedited copy before making separately documented revisions. Resolve the seed, version and candidate-language issues with the source records before using this text in a report.

Export Markdown saves both sections and the run digest as an appendix. Choose a new filename; here it is explicitly labelled unreviewed. The genuine Save action creates the file, and our check confirms that its prose and structured digest match the screen. Successful file export is not scientific approval.

Draft with AI is optional and is not used in this recording. It sends the digest to the configured provider; review its contents and privacy first. A number check cannot decide whether a sentence means the right thing. Python offers build_digest, render_methods and render_results for the same reporting workflow, with the same need for review.
